<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{main}
 For any two   non-isomorphic graphs  $H_1$ and $H_2$ and  any  positive integer $k$,   $\mathcal{R}^k(H_1) \neq \mathcal{R}^k(H_2)$ and $\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H_1) \neq \mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H_2)$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
Let $H$ be a graph and $q$ be an integer at least $3$.  Consider an  $|H|$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ of girth at least $q$ and chromatic number at least $k+1$. The existence of such a graph was first shown by Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal \cite{EH}.
 Let $G=G(H, q, k)$ be a graph on vertex set $V(\mathcal{H})$ that is a union of $|E(\mathcal{H})|$ copies of $H$ induced by respective hyperedges of $\mathcal{H}$. 
 We have that $G\in \mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$ since any vertex-colouring of $G$ in $k$ colours  and thus of $\mathcal{H}$ results in a monochromatic hyperedge of $\mathcal{H}$, i.e., a monochromatic induced copy of $H$. Note that this copy is indeed induced since the girth condition ensures that any two hyperedges of $\mathcal{H}$ intersect in at most one vertex.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{repetition}
For any $k\geq 1$, a  graph has the Ramsey repetition property if and only if it is connected.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Fix $k\geq 1$.

Assume that $H$ is connected. Let $q\geq1$. If $A\in\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$, then clearly $q A\in\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$.
If $A\not\in\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$, repeat a colouring of $A$ without a monochromatic $H$ 
on its disjoint copies. This implies that $q A\not \in\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$. Therefore $H$ has a Ramsey repetition property.

Let $H$  be disconnected and have components $H_1,\ldots,H_t$, where $t\geq2$. Let
$L=H_1\vee\cdots\vee H_t$. Choose
$A\in\mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(L)$ with $ \alpha(A)=\alpha(L)$.     Since $\alpha(A)=\alpha(L)=\max_i\alpha(H_i)<\sum_i\alpha(H_i)=\alpha(H)$,
$A$ contains no induced $H$, thus  $A\not\in \mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$. 
Consider  an arbitrary $k$-vertex colouring of $qA$, for $q=k(t-1)+1$.
Each copy of $A$ contains a  monochromatic
$L$, and $t$ of these have the same colour. Taking $H_i$ from the $i$th
of these $t$ distinct copies gives a monochromatic induced $H$.
Therefore $qA \in \mathcal{R}_{ind}^k(H)$.
Thus $H$ has no Ramsey repetition property.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
